decisions.question: Remove the sample walkthrough (`#demo`: a form with Task title, Date, Time, Priority and a note, then a pretend saved task you can tick), or keep a trimmed one? Removing a demo is your call.
findings: WEB-4 (part: the menu's ‘See an example’ item)
WEB-12 (part: server messages that name the walkthrough)
WEB-18 (part: a static example for visitors without JavaScript)
decisions.recommendation: Remove it (review H, WEB-6). It copies the app's editor and task list, which the site isn't meant to provide (‘the site teaches; the app provides’); its examples are dated September 2026; its green microphone does nothing; and the live demo, now right under the hero, teaches the real loop. In its place, add one static example inside the live demo's intro, laid out as the app shows it, with no inputs: the spoken “Tomorrow, call the dentist and buy bread.” and its two task cards. It shows without JavaScript and whenever the live demo can't run, and the four messages that point to ‘the sample walkthrough’ point to it instead. If you keep the walkthrough (review F, WEB-108): drop its Priority field and ‘· High priority’, make its dates relative to today, delete ‘a sample week in September 2026’ and its fake microphone, and translate it. Until you answer, it stays as it is, in English on the Spanish and Catalan homes too, with a ‘See an example’ item in the menu.

decisions.question: Publish the free plan and TaskFlow Pro on the site now? Saying what's free is your call. Today the site says nothing about it, and its FAQ only says launch pricing isn't announced.
findings: WEB-7 (part: a free-plan line after the demo's hand-over)
WEB-11 (part: a free-plan strip where the bar was)
decisions.recommendation: Yes, without a price, and without ‘100 MB’ until that's final. On dev, accounts without Pro get 10 dictations a month (one dictation can hold several tasks) and can always add tasks by hand with the form, with no limit; TaskFlow Pro is a monthly subscription with unlimited dictation and file space. The new hero says ‘say it’; leaving out that there are 10 a month hides a limit the app shows as soon as they're used (review F: PR-2, TR-2). Where: the FAQ answer `Is TaskFlow free?` (review F's copy, minus its 100 MB clause), one line in the closing card (`Free: 10 dictations a month, and tasks by hand with no limit. TaskFlow Pro: unlimited dictation.`) and one line after the demo's hand-over (`In the app you get 10 free dictations a month, and you can add tasks by hand any time.`), all three in English, Spanish and Catalan from the reports. Until you answer, the FAQ keeps today's answer, which is still true.

decisions.question: Which app screen should the hero show, and the link preview with it? Reviews H and F disagree, and the new images have to be rendered from the app by the main session (Flutter previews with chosen text): today's `App/build` renders hold test text.
findings: WEB-302 (part: an app screen in the preview image)
decisions.recommendation: The Calendar with the hero card's example done: ‘Call the dentist’ and ‘Buy bread’ on tomorrow, under the week strip, with the one «Añadir tarea» button. One image per language and theme (6 PNGs, at the `App/build` size of 780 × 1688), and alt text that says exactly that. It proves the H1 (‘it's on your calendar’), shows what the spoken sentence becomes (review H: one input and the tasks it becomes) and shows the one button a newcomer has to find (review F: what the site shows first, the app shows first). Review H's alternative is the result sheet (‘2 things to add’, ‘Add 2 tasks’); review F's is the Calendar with today's tasks, in English only. decisions.question: Which language should a first visit to the bare address (`/`) get? Today it's always English. This plan adds `/es/` and `/ca/`, with a language switch in the header, the phone menu and the footer.
decisions.recommendation: Choose on `/` only, from the browser's language (Spanish → `/es/`, Catalan → `/ca/`), never from the IP address, falling back to English; and never redirect a visitor who chose a language in the switch (remember that choice in the browser, as the theme is, and add it to privacy §8 with WD3). Spanish- and Catalan-speaking newcomers will mostly get the bare address on WhatsApp, and on a phone the switch sits inside the menu (review G). If you'd rather the site stored nothing more, keep `/` English: the switch is there.

decisions.question: Keep “A little focus. A little flow.” as TaskFlow's brand line in the footer? After this plan it appears nowhere else: the hero, the link preview and the description drop it.
decisions.recommendation: Drop it (review G). It doesn't say what TaskFlow is, and in Spanish and Catalan it either stays English or loses its sound. Review H asked whether you want it as the brand. Until you answer, it stays in the footer, in English, on every page.

decisions.question: Say ‘for Android phones’ and nothing more until an iPhone version is decided, and remove the Apple mentions from the legal pages?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. The delete page links to ‘Manage Apple subscriptions’ and speaks of ‘your Google or Apple account’, and the terms and privacy pages mention Apple payments, but there's no iPhone app. This plan already says ‘An app for Android phones’ (true today, and it doesn't rule out an iPhone version) and drops the FAQ's ‘first testing platform’. Editing the legal pages also needs WD3. The app itself says ‘available in the Android and iOS app’ (`App/lib/l10n/app_en.arb:1695`): fix that through `/ux`.

decisions.question: How should the live demo compare with the free app? It uses Gemini Flash-Lite on Vertex, while the app's dictations use the free AI Studio model by default (UX-616 is open); and it gives 3 tries a day per browser with no account, up to about 90 a month, while the free app gives 10 dictations a month.
decisions.recommendation: Keep the demo as it is for now: this plan labels its tries as the demo's (‘3 tries a day · no sign-up’) and says nothing there is saved to the app. Once UX-616 settles the app's route, give the demo the same route, so it's never faster or more accurate than the app people install (FN-4). Nothing in this plan waits on it.

decisions.question: Should visitors be able to hear when TaskFlow launches?
decisions.recommendation: Not yet: this plan says ‘coming soon to Google Play’ in plain text and offers the live demo. Once the package ID is final (`com.example.agenda` must change before the first upload), use Google Play pre-registration: the same `details?id=` link, a 90-day window per country, and a personal developer account created after 13 November 2023 first needs a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days. An email list would add a form, consent, stored addresses and a privacy update.

decisions.question: Add a section on sharing with family, with a real screenshot of a shared project («Creada por», the filter by person), in the space the appearance section frees?
decisions.recommendation: Not now: subtract first. This plan rewrites the FAQ's sharing answer (WEB-107). Revisit once testers have seen the new home.

decisions.question: The app links to neither the privacy policy nor the terms. Play's User Data policy asks for a privacy-policy link or text inside the app, and Terms §1 says the terms are available before an account is created, but sign-up shows none. Add them? It's an app change, for `/ux`.
decisions.recommendation: Yes: a ‘Privacy’ and a ‘Terms’ link on the sign-up screen and in the app's settings, opening the site's pages in the app's language (`/es/privacy/` and so on). Run it through `/ux`.

decisions.question: Two facts only you can give, for the privacy and delete pages: how long backups keep deleted data (the pages promise only ‘the provider's rolling window’), and whether the app's dictations use a paid Gemini key or the free quota.
decisions.recommendation: Give both when you can. With a number, both pages can say ‘Backups are deleted within N days’, which Play asks for; with paid or EEA terms, privacy §4 can say plainly that Google doesn't use dictations to train its models. Both edits go with WD3.

decisions.question: At release: publish the site only together with, or after, the app and backend it describes? And which deletion URL goes into Play Console?
decisions.recommendation: Publish them together. The site will describe in-app deletion, email codes, several tasks per dictation and voice commands: all on dev, none deployed, and testers' APK 1.0.5 and staging predate them. For Play Console, `/delete-account/` (review G): its first control is the language switch. Review L suggested `/es/delete-account/`. Decide with the package ID.
